analyticalQuestion: At fixed small coupling A_q=delta q^2, do the certified and finite retained-coset ledgers display the q^6 data scale, q^2 prescribed atom-proxy scale, q-independent one-third endpoint proxy, and delta^(4/3) collapse?
takeaway: The source certificates give D proportional to q^6 and the complete prescribed atomProxy sum proportional to q^2. Their atomProxy/D^(1/3) endpoint ratio is q-independent to the recorded accuracy, and the high-precision delta sweep has fitted power 4/3. The separate finite retained-coset charge and truncation diagnostics remain explicitly segregated from the analytic proxy.

filled circles, open squares, open diamonds, and open triangles

panels.A: fixed-delta retained-coset D and complete prescribed atomProxy sum indexed to q=256
panels.B: high-precision endpoint proxies and separately integrated finite retained-coset endpoint proxy and full retained charge upper bound

claimBoundary: The figure extracts values from the committed R0.71X certificates. The atomProxy is not the multiplier-locked J_* atom; the missing fixed multiplier and kappa factor are not instantiated numerically. The retained-coset calculation is finite-dimensional corroboration, not DNS, and does not prove spectral convergence. The continuum implicit-function theorem provides an existential small-coupling radius, but delta=1/128 has not been proved to lie inside that radius. The figure proves no universal D^(1/3) estimate and no Navier-Stokes regularity statement.
